newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Bruce Springsteen wins Sweden's Polar Prize.
newsitem.headline: Bruce Springsteen wins Sweden's Polar Prize.

text.p: American rock star Bruce "The Boss" Springsteen won one of the world's most valuable music prizes, Sweden's 1997 Polar Prize, on Wednesday.
The sixth annual Polar Prize, worth one million Swedish crowns ($144,000), was won jointly by Springsteen and Swedish choral conductor Eric Ericson.
It will be presented by Sweden's King Carl XVI Gustaf at a ceremony in Stockholm on May 5.
Announcing the award to Springsteen, the prize committee said his authority in rock music was unshakeable.
"In a world of music where styles are fluctuating all the time, Bruce Springsteen stands with both feet firmly planted on the ground of rock 'n' roll," the committee said in a statement.
"He stands up straight and hits hard but he does so with discretion and not without tenderness."
Springsteen, 47, has remained at the top of the world's music business since his 1984 album "Born In The USA".
His most recent album, "The Ghost of Tom Joad", was voted one of the best 10 albums of 1995.
Eric Ericson, 78, who created Sweden's first professional choral group in 1946, was awarded the prize for his achievements as a conductor, teacher, and for his leading role in Swedish music.

The Polar Prize was set up in 1992 by Stikkan Anderson, former manager of the hugely successful Swedish pop group, Abba, through a 42 million crown ($6.1 million) endowment that is now worth an estimated 60 million crowns.

It was first presented in 1992 to Paul McCartney of the Beatles and has since been won by a list of international stars including Joni Mitchell, Elton John, Quincy Jones and posthumously by Dizzy Gillespie. ($1=6.9539 Swedish crowns)
